parts.problem_md: The three roots of $\mathrm{p} ( x ) = 0$ , where $\mathrm{p} ( x ) = 2 x^{3} + a x^{2} + b x + c$ are $x=\frac{1}{2},x=n$ and $x=-n$, where $a,b,c$ and $n$ are integers. The $y$-intercept of the graph of $y=p(x)$ is 4. Find $p(x)$, simplifying your coefficients.
parts.solution_md:
> *The *$y$*-intercept is 4 and this occurs when *$x=0$* *

> *Substitute *$x=0$* into *$\mathrm{p} ( x )$

$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = 2 ( 0 )^{3} + a ( 0 )^{2} + b ( 0 ) + c$

$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = c = 4$

> *Rewrite the polynomial*

*(1)      *$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = 2 x^{3} + a x^{2} + b x + 4$

> *Use the given roots to factorise the polynomial*

$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = ( x + n ) ( x - n ) ( 2 x - 1 )$

**[1]**

> *Expand the first 2 brackets*

$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = ( x^{2} - x n + x n - n^{2} ) ( 2 x - 1 )$

> *Simplify*

$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = ( x^{2} - n^{2} ) ( 2 x - 1 )$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets*

*(2)     ** *$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = 2 x^{3} - x^{2} - 2 n^{2} x + n^{2}$

**[1]**

> *(1) and (2) are the same cubic so:*

> *Compare constants:*

$4=n^{2}$

**[1]**

$n=\pm2$

> *Compare coefficients of *$x^{2}$

$a=-1$

> *Compare coefficients of *$x$

$b=-2n^{2}=-2\times2^{2}=-8$

> *Write down *$\mathrm{p} ( x )$

$p(x)=2x^{3}-x^{2}-8x+4$ **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
$p(x)=ax^{3}+3x^{2}+bx-12$ has a factor of $2x+1$. When $p(x)$ is divided by $x-3$ the remainder is 105.

Find the value of $a$ and of $b$.
parts.solution_md:
> *By the factor theorem, if *$2x+1$* is a factor, then *$\mathrm{p} ( - 1 \frac{1}{2} ) = 0$* [this is obtained by solving *$2x+1=0$* to get *$x=-\frac{1}{2}$*]*

> *Substitute this into the polynomial*

$\mathrm{p} ( - 1 \frac{1}{2} ) = a ( - 1 \frac{1}{2} )^{3} + 3 ( - 1 \frac{1}{2} )^{2} + b ( - 1 \frac{1}{2} ) - 12 = 0$

$-\frac{1}{8}a+\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{2}b-12=0$

> *Multiply through by 8*

$-a+6-4b-96=0$

> *Collect the constant term on one side*

$a+4b=-90$

**[1]**

> $p ( 3 ) = 105$* so use this to make a second equation*

$\mathrm{p} ( 3 ) = a ( 3 )^{3} + 3 ( 3 )^{2} + b ( 3 ) - 12 = 105$

**[1]**

$27a+27+3b-12=105$

$27a+3b=90$

$9a+b=30$

**[1]**

> *Now we have two equations which we can solve simultaneously*

$a+4b=-90$

$9a+b=30$

> *Multiply the second equation by 4 and then subtract the equations*

$a+4b=-90$

$36a+4b=120$

> *Subtracting gives*

$35a=210$

$a=6$

> *Find b*

$b = 30 - ( 9 \times 6 ) = - 24$

$a=6,b=-24$** [2]**

The polynomial $p(x)=6x^{3}+ax^{2}+bx+2$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers, has a factor of $x--2$ . 
Given that $p(1)=--2p(0)$, find the values of $a$ and $b$.
parts.solution_md:
> *In this question you need to use the information given to form and then solve two linear simultaneous equations*

> $p(x)$* has a factor *$(x-2)$*, so from the factor theorem we know *$x=2$* is a solution of*$p(x)=0$*. Substitute *$x=2$*into *$p(x)=0$

$6 ( 2 )^{3} + a ( 2 )^{2} + b ( 2 ) + 2 = 0$

> *Now simplify to get an equation in terms of*$a$* and *$b$*. *

$6\times8+4a+2b+2=0\,48+4a+2b+2=0$

**[1]**

> *We can also collect like terms and pass the constant term to the right hand side*

$4a+2b=-50$

> *As all the terms are even, we can also divide both sides by 2*

$2 a + b = - 25 \textcircled{1}$

> *We now have one of two simultaneous equations*

> *To get the other, use "p(1) = -2p(0)". Substitute 1 into p to get p(1), substitute 0 into p to get p(0)  *

$\begin{gathered} \mathrm{p} ( 1 ) & = 6 ( 1 )^{3} + a ( 1 )^{2} + b ( 1 ) + 2 \\ = 6 + a + b + 2 \\ = 8 + a + b \\ \\ \mathrm{p} ( 0 ) & = 6 ( 0 )^{3} + a ( 0 )^{2} + b ( 0 ) + 2 \\ = 2 \end{gathered}$

> *p(1) = -2p(0) so equate p(1) to negative two times p(0)*

$\begin{gathered} 8 + a + b & = - 2 \times 2 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify this and pass the constants to the right hand side to get the second of the two simultaneous equations*

$\begin{gathered} 8 + a + b & = - 4 \\ a + b & = - 12 \textcircled{2} \end{gathered}$

> *Solve the simultaneous equations by elimination as below or by substitution; whichever method you feel most comfortable with!*

$\begin{gathered} 2 a + b & = - 25 \textcircled{1} \\ a + b & = - 12 \textcircled{2} \end{gathered}$

> *Subtract *`circle enclose 2`* from *`circle enclose 1`*, taking care with the negative numbers*

$\begin{gathered} \textcircled{1} - \textcircled{2} : a & = - 13 \end{gathered}$

**any valid attempt to solve simultaneous equations ****[1]**

> *And substitute *$a=-13$* into *`circle enclose 1`* or *`circle enclose 2`* (*`circle enclose 2`* is easier) to obtain *$a$

$\begin{gathered} a + b & = - 12 \\ - 13 + b & = - 12 \\ b = 1 \end{gathered}$

> *Make sure that both the values of *$a$* and *$b$* are clearly written.*

$a=-13,b=1$** [1]**

(i) Show that $x+2$ is a factor of $p(x)$ .

parts.solution_md:
i) *Using the factor theorem, if *$x-a$* is a factor of *$\mathrm{f} ( x )$*, then *$\mathrm{f} ( a ) = 0$*    *

$\mathrm{p} ( - 2 ) = 15 ( - 2 )^{3 } + 22 ( - 2 )^{2} - 15 ( - 2 ) + 2$

> *Simplifying each term   *

$p(-2)=-120+88+30+2$

$p(-2)=0$ **[1]**

ii) *If *$x+2$* is a factor then factorising by inspection or using polynomial division gives*

`long division by x + 2 yields 15 x ^2 none - 8 x none + 1 none pile 15 x ^3 none + 22 x ^2 none - 15 x none + 2 15 x ^3 none + 30 x ^2 none - 15 x none + 2 none - horizontal line none none none none none - 8 x ^2 none - 15 x none none none none none none - 8 x ^2 none - 16 x none none none none - horizontal line none none none none none none none none none none none none x none + 2 none none none none none none none none none none none none x none + 2 none - horizontal line none none none none none none none none none none none none none none none 0 end pile end long division`

> *  *

$( x + 2 ) ( 15 x^{2 } - 8 x + 1 )$

**correct method to find the quadratic factor** **[1]**

**fully correct quadratic factor**** [1]**

> *Factorising the second bracket*

> *We need a pair of numbers that for *$ax^{2}+bx+c$*, multiply to *$ac$* and add to *$b$*. In this case this is -3 and -5. *

> *Rewrite the middle term using *$-3x$* and *$-5x$

$15x^{2}-3x-5x+1$

> *Group and factorise the first two terms, using *$3x$* as the highest common factor, and group and factorise the second two terms, using -1 as the factor*

$3 x ( 5 x - 1 ) - 1 ( 5 x - 1 )$

> *Note that these terms now have a common factor of *$( 5 x - 1 )$* so this whole bracket can be factorised out, leaving *$3x-1$* in its own bracket.*

> *This means that the quadratic factorises to *

$( 3 x - 1 ) ( 5 x - 1 )$

> *Therefore, the cubic factorises to*

$(x+2)(3x-1)(5x-1)$ **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
The polynomial $p(x)=ax^{3}+bx^{2}-19x+4$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants, has a factor $x+4$ and is such that $2p(1)=5p(0)$.

Show that $p(x)=(x+4)(Ax^{2}+Bx+C)$, where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are integers to be found.
parts.solution_md:
> *Find *$\mathrm{p} ( 1 )$*.*

$\mathrm{p} ( 1 ) = a ( 1 )^{3} + b ( 1 )^{2} - 19 ( 1 ) + 4
 \mathrm{p} ( 1 ) = a + b - 15$

> *Therefore,*

$2 \mathrm{p} ( 1 ) = 2 a + 2 b - 30$

> *Find *$\mathrm{p} ( 0 )$*.*

$\mathrm{p} ( 0 ) = 4$

> *Therefore,*

$5 \mathrm{p} ( 0 ) = 20$

> *We are told that *$2 \mathrm{p} ( 1 ) = 5 \mathrm{p} ( 0 )$*.*

> *Therefore,*

$\begin{gathered} 2 a + 2 b - 30 & = 20 \\ \\ a + b - 15 & = 10 \\ \\ a + b - 25 & = 0 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *We are told that *$( x + 4 )$* is a factor of *$\mathrm{p} ( x )$*. Using factor theorem, this means that *$\mathrm{p} ( - 4 ) = 0$*.*

`equation`

> *Divide through by 16.*

$\begin{gathered} - 4 a + b + 5 & = 0 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *We now have two equations in terms of *$a$* and *$b$*. Solve simultaneously. *

> * *

$\begin{gathered} - 4 a + b + 5 & = a + b - 25 \\ - 5 a & = - 30 \\ a = 6 \end{gathered}$

> *Substitute into one of the equations to find a value for *$b$*.*

> * *

$\begin{gathered} - 4 ( 6 ) + b + 5 & = 0 \\ b - 19 & = 0 \\ b = 19 \end{gathered}$

> *  *

**1 mark for each value ****[2]**

> *Substituting these values into the polynomial,*

$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = 6 x^{3} + 19 x^{2} - 19 x + 4$

> *  *

> *We know one of the factors of the polynomial is *$( x + 4 )$*. We can find the missing quadratic factor by inspection.*

> *  *

$6 x^{3} + 19 x^{2} - 19 x + 4 = ( x + 4 ) ( A x^{2} + B x + C )$

> *  *

> $A$* must be 6 to achieve the *$6x^{3}$*. *$C$* must be 1 to achieve the 4.*

> *  *

$6 x^{3} + 19 x^{2} - 19 x + 4 = ( x + 4 ) ( 6 x^{2} + B x + 1 )$

**[1]**

> *  *

> *When expanded, the *$x^{2}$* terms are *$( 4 \times 6 x^{2} )$* and *$( x \times B x )$*. Sum and equate to *$19x^{2}$*.*

> * *

$( 24 + B ) x^{2} = 19 x^{2}$

> * *

> *Therefore,*

$\begin{gathered} 24 + B & = 19 \\ B = - 5 \end{gathered}$

> *  *

$(x+4)(6x^{2}-5x+1)$** **$[ 1 ]$

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

The polynomial p(x) = ax³ + bx² - 19x + 4, where a and b are constants, has a factor x + 4 and is such that 2p(1) = 5p(0).

From part a, we found that a = 6 and b = 19, giving:
p(x) = 6x³ + 19x² - 19x + 4

And we showed that:
p(x) = (x + 4)(Ax² + Bx + C)

where A = 6, B = -5, and C = 1.

Therefore:
p(x) = (x + 4)(6x² - 5x + 1)

Hence factorise $p(x)$.

a = 6
b = 19

parts.solution_md:

$\mathrm{p} ' ( x ) = 18 x^{2} + 38 x - 19$

> *When *$\mathrm{p} ' ( x )$* is divided by *$x$*, we substitute 0 into the equation.*

$\mathrm{p} ' ( 0 ) = 18 ( 0 )^{2} + 38 ( 0 ) - 19
 \mathrm{p} ' ( 0 ) = - 19$

$p(x)$ has a remainder of 11 when divided by $x-3$ and a remainder of $-21$ when divided by $x+1$. 
Given that $p(x)=(x-2)Q(x)$, find $Q(x)$, a quadratic factor with numerical coefficients.
parts.solution_md:
> *Using remainder theorem, *$\mathrm{p} ( 3 ) = 11$* and *$\mathrm{p} ( - 1 ) = - 21$*.*

$\begin{gathered} 6 ( 3 )^{3} + a ( 3 )^{2} + 12 ( 3 ) + b & = 11 \\ \\ 6 ( - 1 )^{3} + a ( - 1 )^{2} + 12 ( - 1 ) + b & = - 21 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange and simplify to get two equations in terms of *$a$* and *$b$*.*

$\begin{gathered} 9 a + b + 187 & = 0 \\ \\ a + b + 3 & = 0 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Solve the simultaneous equations.*

> *For example, by multiplying the second equation by 9 and using the elimination method.*

> *  *

`Error converting from MathML to accessible text.`

*  ***[1]**

> *Substitute *$b=20$* into one of the equations to find *$a$*.*

$\begin{gathered} a + 20 + 3 & = 0 \\ a = - 23 \end{gathered}$

* *** ****[1]**

$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = 6 x^{3} - 23 x^{2} + 12 x + 20$

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

p(x) = 6x³ + ax² + 12x + b, where a and b are integers.

p(x) has a remainder of 11 when divided by x - 3 and a remainder of -21 when divided by x + 1.

Given that p(x) = (x - 2)Q(x), find Q(x), a quadratic factor with numerical coefficients.

Using remainder theorem and solving simultaneous equations: a = -23 and b = 20.

Therefore p(x) = 6x³ - 23x² + 12x + 20

Using algebraic long division:

p(x) = (x - 2)(6x² - 11x - 10)

Hence solve $p(x)=0$.
parts.solution_md:
> *Factorise *$6x^{2}-11x-10$* in order to write *$\mathrm{p} ( x )$* as the product of three linear factors.*

$6 x^{2} - 11 x - 10 = ( 3 x + 2 ) ( 2 x - 5 )$

**[1]**

> *Therefore,*

$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = ( x - 2 ) ( 3 x + 2 ) ( 2 x - 5 )$

> *When *$\mathrm{p} ( x ) = 0$

$( x - 2 ) ( 3 x + 2 ) ( 2 x - 5 ) = 0$

> *Solve.*

$x=2,x=-\frac{2}{3},x=\frac{5}{2}$* ***[1]**
